stories.headline: Broadcom AI chip revenue jumps 106% to $8.4B, projects over $100B in AI sales by 2027
key_facts: Broadcom reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $2.05 beating the $2.03 estimate, with revenue of $19.31 billion up 29% year-over-year
AI chip revenue reached $8.4 billion, a 106% year-over-year increase driven by demand for custom accelerators and AI networking
CEO Hock Tan said the company has 'line of sight to achieve AI revenue from chips, just chips, in excess of $100 billion in 2027'
Guidance for Q2 expects revenue of approximately $22 billion, well above the $20.56 billion analyst consensus
Broadcom disclosed hyperscaler custom chip deployment plans: OpenAI projected to deploy over 1 GW of custom processors in 2027, Meta planning multiple gigawatts of MTIA accelerator capacity
The company announced a new $10 billion share buyback program; shares rose 4% in after-hours trading

sources.title: Broadcom's AI chip business jumps 106% as it cruises to another solid earnings and revenue beat

stories.headline: Tesla seeks to more than double AI6 chip production at Samsung's 2nm foundry
key_facts: Tesla is negotiating with Samsung to increase AI6 chip production from approximately 16,000 wafers per month to around 40,000 wafers per month
The AI6 chip will be manufactured on Samsung's 2-nanometer process, an advancement from the previous HW4 chip made on a 5nm node
Tesla's long-term foundry agreement with Samsung covers AI6 production through December 31, 2033, valued at approximately 22.8 trillion won ($16-17 billion)
AI6 will power Tesla's Full Self-Driving autonomous system, the Optimus humanoid robot, and internal AI data centers
Industry sources indicate AI6 clusters could potentially replace functions previously planned for Tesla's Dojo supercomputer
Tesla purchasing executives were scheduled to meet Samsung officials this week to finalize expansion terms

stories.headline: Vertiv and Generate Capital launch 'Bring Your Own Power & Cooling' model for data centers
key_facts: Vertiv and Generate Capital announced a strategic collaboration to deliver complete Bring Your Own Power & Cooling (BYOP&C) solutions for US data centers
The model combines Vertiv's power and cooling infrastructure with Generate's financing, asset ownership, and operational expertise
Initial deployments target North American markets with constrained grid access, using reciprocating engines, turbines, fuel cells, battery storage, and alternative energy
The collaboration addresses two key constraints: grid connection delays and high upfront infrastructure capital requirements
Generate's financing model reduces or eliminates upfront customer infrastructure investment while preserving future grid-connection optionality
Vertiv will provide modular, fully converged building blocks designed to shorten design cycles and standardize deployment

sources.title: Vertiv and Generate Capital Collaborate to Accelerate Data Center Capacity with Complete Power and Cooling Infrastructure

stories.headline: UK GPU datacenter demonstrates 40% AI power reduction on demand in National Grid trial
key_facts: A London GPU datacenter operated by Nebius achieved a 40% reduction in AI power consumption during a five-day trial in December 2025, results published March 4
The trial involved Nebius, National Grid, Emerald AI, and EPRI's Datacenter Flexible Load Initiative
Over 200 simulated grid event notifications were tested across a 130 kW compute cluster running Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs
Power flexibility was achieved by pausing or deprioritizing GPU jobs and shifting workloads, not by powering down equipment
AI training workloads including GPT, Llama, and Qwen models proved suitable due to natural checkpoint intervals where processing can pause
The trial achieved 100% compliance with all requested power reduction targets and ramp rates
National Grid Partners president Steve Smith said 'High-performance datacenters don't have to place additional strain on the grid'

sources.title: Flex appeal: UK datacenter cuts AI power draw 40% on command

stories.headline: Seven tech giants sign White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge to self-fund data center power
key_facts: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, and xAI signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge at the White House on March 4
Companies committed to build, bring, or buy new generation resources and cover all power delivery infrastructure upgrades for their data centers
Signatories will negotiate new separate rate structures with utilities and state governments wherever they build data centers
Companies agreed to pay these rates whether or not they use the electricity, ensuring costs are not passed to American households
The pledge includes commitments to hire and train workers from communities where data centers operate
Companies will coordinate with grid operators to make backup generation resources available, contributing to grid reliability
The signing took place in the Indian Treaty Room of the Eisenhower Executive Office Building

sources.title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Advances Energy Affordability with the Ratepayer Protection Pledge

stories.headline: NTSB finds Waymo remote operator told robotaxi to illegally pass stopped school bus in Austin
key_facts: The NTSB published a preliminary report on a January 12, 2026 incident where a Waymo robotaxi illegally passed a stopped school bus in Austin, Texas
The autonomous system functioned correctly by stopping and asking its remote human operator 'Is this a school bus with active signals?' — the operator responded 'No' and the vehicle proceeded
The illegal pass prompted five other human-driven vehicles to follow suit, compounding the safety risk for students
Waymo issued a voluntary software recall on 3,000 vehicles to address school bus detection issues
Austin ISD has asked Waymo to cease operations during morning and afternoon school hours when students use buses
Under Texas Transportation Code Section 545.066, drivers must remain stopped until a school bus deactivates its signals

stories.headline: South Korea's M.AX Alliance targets top-3 global humanoid robot status, 1,000 units by 2029
key_facts: South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources convened a special meeting of the Manufacturing AI Alliance (M.AX) on March 5 to discuss humanoid robot competitiveness
Participants included Hyundai Motor, Robros, Yuil Robotics, and robotics experts from research institutes and academia
The alliance aims to develop a foundation AI model for humanoid robots for industrial use by 2028 and begin producing at least 1,000 robots annually from 2029
Government officials discussed independent development of core robot equipment and streamlining of regulations to reach top-3 global status
Global humanoid robot sales surpassed $500 million for the first time in 2025, with the market expected to reach $4.4 billion by 2027
Ministry director Kim Sung-yeol said 'humanoid robots will soon become the new battleground among global big tech companies'

stories.headline: Japan's Space One Kairos rocket fails for third consecutive time, self-destructs 69 seconds after liftoff
key_facts: Space One's Kairos No. 3 rocket self-destructed 68.8 seconds after liftoff from Spaceport Kii on March 5, after the flight termination system activated
About 70 seconds after liftoff an energetic event became visible in the rocket's plume with several fragments including one large tumbling piece
The first-stage engine burn had carried the 18-meter, 23-ton solid-fuel rocket to an altitude of about 29 kilometers before termination
The rocket was carrying five experimental satellites from Japanese companies and the Taiwan Space Agency
Space One suggested a malfunction in the safety system that automatically determines flight termination may have occurred
This was the third consecutive failure: Kairos No. 1 exploded after liftoff in March 2024, No. 2 self-destructed in December 2024
Reuters reported the failure 'leaves Japan without commercial launch capability,' highlighting reliance on American rockets amid space-security concerns

stories.headline: Spain's PLD Space raises $209M led by Mitsubishi Electric to scale Miura-5 rocket production
key_facts: PLD Space closed a €180 million ($209 million) Series C round, the largest funding round for a European space business announced in 2026
The round was led by Japanese satellite maker Mitsubishi Electric, which secured priority launch access for missions in the Asian market
Total financing raised exceeds €350 million since the company was founded in 2011 in Elche, Spain
Miura-5 is a reusable small satellite launcher with its first orbital test flight targeted for 2026 and commercial services planned for 2027
PLD Space aims to exceed 30 launches per year by 2030; first commercial contract signed with Sateliot for two direct-to-device satellites
PLD Space launched Europe's first fully private rocket (suborbital Miura 1) in 2023
